headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Ordering and Installing a New Bathroom Countertop
articleBody:
Upgrading your vanity top requires accuracy from fabrication through final sealing. Here are frequent mistakes clients encounter and practical ways to avoid them:

1. Measuring the old countertop instead of the cabinet: Old tops often feature irregular overhangs. Measure the actual cabinet box dimensions, adding specific overhang allowances to fit your layout.
2. Templating over an unlevel cabinet: Fabricating a top to fit an unlevel base creates high spots that crack stone. Ensure the vanity is shimmed and anchored before templating occurs.
3. Installing the faucet after setting the slab: Connecting supply lines and faucet nuts inside a cramped vanity cabinet is difficult. Mount the faucet and drain assembly to the countertop before lowering it into place.
4. Rushing the adhesive cure time: Hooking up plumbing lines or filling sinks before adhesives and silicone set—often requiring up to 24 to 48 hours—can break the seal and create slow leaks.
5. Skipping a dry fit: Setting adhesive before checking how the slab sits against the wall and plumbing cutouts leads to rushed fixes. Always dry-fit the top first.
6. Mismatched sink cutouts: Ordering a top without matching sink rim specs can ruin the reveal. Confirm exact sink templates prior to stone fabrication.
